meta.expect: reaches rung 2 by teacher turn 16, never concedes

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll type END MEETING on its own line, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Mr. Hale. You asked for this meeting, so I'm here. I have a client call at 4:40. Tell me why my son has a zero in your gradebook.

Thanks for coming in, Ms. Kalinowski. I called this meeting, and before anything else I owe you one thing: the zero went into the gradebook before I called home. That was wrong of me, and I'm sorry Owen found out that way.
Okay. Go on.
I want to show you what I'm looking at, and I'd like you to check it yourself.
Show me. Turn the screen toward me.

This is the version history of Owen's essay. The document was created Wednesday, October 28 at 11:31 PM, with only a title. At 11:52, 612 words appear in a single edit. At 11:58, another 794 words in a single edit.
Eleven fifty-two. Eleven fifty-eight. Say the times again, slowly, and I'll write them down.
There are no earlier drafts anywhere in the history.
"No earlier drafts." I'm writing that down. Does the history show anything before 11:31 PM on the twenty-eighth, or does it start there?
On October 15 he handed in his outline. It argued Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues 'epistemological paralysis' and never mentions cowardice.
Cowardice in October. Paralysis in the essay. Did he change his argument, or did someone else write a different one?
The essay quotes Act 3, Scene 2: 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' That line is not in Hamlet. You can search the play yourself.
Then that's an invented quotation, cited to a scene. Did Owen know it was made up, or did he think it was real? Be precise, Hale.
I'm not calling Owen a liar. I'm telling you what the document shows.
"I'm not calling Owen a liar." Good. Then don't let the document say it for you. What does it show about who wrote the essay?
Here's his in-class writing from September 24 next to it.
Put them side by side. I want to see them.
The school's policy for a first concern is a supervised rewrite. If the rewrite holds up, nothing goes on his record.

Wait. You're offering a rewrite after you've already put a zero in the book? Procedure 4.2 says you call me before any mark goes in. Nobody called me. My son found out from his phone, in front of his class.
He would do it at lunch in my room, not in front of the class.
Private is better. It doesn't fix the zero, and it doesn't fix the phone. Put in writing that nothing goes on his record, and that the zero comes off before the rewrite, not after.
What would you need from me to be comfortable with that?
You're asking me what I need. I need the zero withdrawn today, in writing, and nothing on his record. Then we can talk about a rewrite. Is that in your power, or do I go to the principal?
I can put that in an email to you tonight.

Tonight isn't enough. The zero comes off before Owen sees the rewrite prompt, and the email says "nothing on file" in those words. Send it to me and the principal, and I'll have it on my desk in the morning.
Is there anything else you want me to include?
Put in an apology to Owen for the phone, from you, by name. And the date you entered the zero, November 3, so there's no confusion about when it happened.
Then I'll send it by eight.
Eight. I'll be reading it. Owen's rewrite is a separate question, and I'm not agreeing to it until I see the email.
Thank you for coming in.
Okay. Eight o'clock.
I'll see Owen tomorrow at lunch.
Not tomorrow. Not before the email. And you say nothing to him about the essay until I've seen it.
